title: The conditional: hablaría, tendría
summary: Would in Spanish: -ía endings on the infinitive, the future's irregular stems, and the conditional for advice, polite requests, daydreams and looking back.
focus: Forming the simple conditional and using it for advice, politeness, hypotheses, past probability and the future seen from the past
content:
## Forms: endings on the infinitive

The conditional is the English *would*, as in **hablaría** (I would speak). Like the future, it keeps the whole infinitive and adds endings, and the endings are the same for -ar, -er and -ir verbs:

| | hablar | comer | vivir |
|---|---|---|---|
| yo | hablaría | comería | viviría |
| tú | hablarías | comerías | vivirías |
| él / ella / usted | hablaría | comería | viviría |
| nosotros/as | hablaríamos | comeríamos | viviríamos |
| vosotros/as | hablaríais | comeríais | viviríais |
| ellos / ellas / ustedes | hablarían | comerían | vivirían |

Every ending carries an accent on the **í**. Don't mix it up with the imperfect. **Comía** means I was eating, and **comería** means I would eat. The yo and él forms are the same, so add **yo** or **él** when it isn't clear.

## Irregular stems: the same as the future

The conditional uses exactly the irregular stems of the future, so you only learn them once.

| infinitive | future | conditional |
|---|---|---|
| tener | tendré | **tendría** |
| venir | vendré | **vendría** |
| poner | pondré | **pondría** |
| salir | saldré | **saldría** |
| saber | sabré | **sabría** |
| haber | habrá | **habría** |
| hacer | haré | **haría** |
| decir | diré | **diría** |

You already know **podría** and **querría**. **Ir** is regular: **iría**. As *there would be*, **habría** has one form only, like **hay**. The six forms of **haber** in the drill are the auxiliary you will use at B2: **habría hecho**.

## Advice and polite requests

To give advice, imagine yourself in the other person's shoes:

- **Yo que tú, saldría antes.** If I were you, I'd leave earlier.
- **Yo en tu lugar, no diría nada.** In your place, I wouldn't say anything.
- **Deberías descansar.** You should rest.

To ask politely, the conditional softens the question:

- **¿Podrías ayudarme?** Could you help me?
- **¿Te importaría esperar un momento?** Would you mind waiting a moment? (The pattern is **¿Te importaría** + infinitive?)
- **¿Tienes un minuto?** becomes **¿Tendrías un minuto?** (Would you have a minute?)

## Wishes and daydreams

**Me encantaría** and **me gustaría** + infinitive say what you would love or like to do:

- **Me encantaría vivir en el campo.** I'd love to live in the countryside.

Imagined situations take the conditional too, with a short phrase instead of an *if*-clause:

- **Con más tiempo, aprendería a cocinar.** With more time, I'd learn to cook.
- **En tu casa, yo pondría un sofá grande.** In your house, I'd put a big sofa.
- **¿Qué harías con un millón de euros?** What would you do with a million euros?

The full *if*-sentence (si tuviera dinero, viajaría…) needs the imperfect subjunctive, which comes at B2.

## Guessing about the past, and the future seen from the past

The future guesses about *now*; the conditional guesses about *then*:

- **Serán las diez.** It's probably about ten (now).
- **Cuando llegó, serían las diez.** When he arrived, it must have been about ten.
- **Habría mucho tráfico.** There must have been a lot of traffic.

When you report a promise or plan made in the past, its future becomes conditional:

- **Dice que vendrá.** In the past it becomes **Dijo que vendría.** He said he would come.
- **Sabía que lo harías.** I knew you would do it.

vocabulary.example: Yo que tú, iría al médico hoy.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If I were you, I'd go to the doctor today.

vocabulary.meaning: in your place, if I were you
vocabulary.example: Yo en tu lugar, no le diría nada.
vocabulary.example_meaning: In your place, I wouldn't tell him anything.
Would you mind speaking more slowly?

vocabulary.example: Mañana te echaría una mano, pero trabajo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'd give you a hand tomorrow, but I'm working.

vocabulary.example: La mudanza sería más fácil con una furgoneta.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The move would be easier with a van.

vocabulary.example: Nos encantaría conocer a tus padres.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We'd love to meet your parents.

vocabulary.example: En el campo viviríamos más tranquilos.
vocabulary.example_meaning: In the countryside we'd live more peacefully.

vocabulary.example: Tardó dos horas: habría un atasco.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It took him two hours: there must have been a traffic jam.

vocabulary.example: Me prometiste que harías la cena.
vocabulary.example_meaning: You promised me you'd make dinner.

vocabulary.example: Dijeron que nos avisarían por la mañana.
vocabulary.example_meaning: They said they'd let us know in the morning.

quiz.prompt: Tienes un problema con tu jefe. Yo que tú, ___ con él.
quiz.explanation: Yo que tú + conditional, in the yo form: hablaría (I would talk). Hablaré is a plan, not advice; hablarías is 'you would'.
hints: The speaker imagines what *I* would do.

quiz.prompt: Yo en tu lugar, ___ (tener) más paciencia.
quiz.explanation: Tener has the same irregular stem as the future (tendré): tendr- + -ía gives tendría.
hints: Stem tendr- plus the yo ending -ía.

quiz.prompt: ¿Te importaría ___ una mano con la mudanza?
quiz.explanation: ¿Te importaría…? is followed by an infinitive, with the pronoun attached: ¿Te importaría echarme una mano?
hints: Would you mind + doing: what form follows?

quiz.explanation: Encantar works like gustar: the thing loved (vivir en el campo) is the subject, so the verb is singular: me encantaría.
hints: Singular: an infinitive is the subject.

quiz.prompt: Anoche Luis no contestó al teléfono. ¿Dónde estaba? ___ en el campo, sin cobertura.
quiz.explanation: A guess about the past uses the conditional, third person: estaría means he was probably. Estaré is 'I will be'; estarías is 'you would be'.
hints: We are guessing about Luis, last night.

quiz.prompt: Ayer Ana me prometió que ___ (venir) a la fiesta, pero al final no vino.
quiz.explanation: A promise made in the past: its future (vendré) becomes the conditional, vendría. Same stem as the future: vendr-.

quiz.prompt: Estoy perdido en la ciudad. ¿Qué ___ tú en mi lugar?
quiz.explanation: Hacer has the short stem har- (haré, haría): ¿Qué harías tú en mi lugar? Hacerías does not exist, and harás asks about your own plans.
hints: Hacer becomes haré in the future.

quiz.prompt: Ayer Juan llegó muy tarde: ___ un atasco en la autopista.
quiz.explanation: A guess about yesterday: the conditional of hay, habría (there must have been). Like hay, it has one form only, so never habrían here; habrá guesses about now.
hints: It's a guess about the past.

quiz.prompt: Me dijiste que me ___ (avisar) al llegar, ¡y no me llamaste!
quiz.explanation: Reporting what 'you' said you would do: avisar + -ías gives avisarías. Regular verbs keep the whole infinitive.

conjugations.meaning: to have (auxiliary verb); habría = there would be

conversations.title: A job in Valencia
conversations.scenario: Javier has been offered a job in another city and asks his friend Lucía what she would do.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Lucía, ¿tendrías cinco minutos? Necesito un consejo.
lines.meaning: Lucía, would you have five minutes? I need some advice.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Me ofrecen un trabajo en Valencia, pero tendría que mudarme.
lines.meaning: They're offering me a job in Valencia, but I'd have to move.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Qué bien! Yo que tú, lo aceptaría sin pensarlo.
lines.meaning: Great! If I were you, I'd accept it without thinking twice.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Ya, pero echaría de menos a mis amigos.
lines.meaning: Yeah, but I'd miss my friends.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Podrías volver los fines de semana. Son solo tres horas en tren.
lines.meaning: You could come back at weekends. It's only three hours by train.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Es verdad. Y me encantaría vivir cerca del mar.
lines.meaning: That's true. And I'd love to live near the sea.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¿Ves? Además, yo te visitaría todos los meses.
lines.meaning: See? Besides, I'd visit you every month.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Les dije que les daría una respuesta el lunes.
lines.meaning: I told them I'd give them an answer on Monday.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Pues yo en tu lugar, los llamaría hoy mismo.
lines.meaning: Well, in your place, I'd call them today.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Vale. ¿Me echarías una mano con la mudanza?
lines.meaning: OK. Would you give me a hand with the move?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Por supuesto! Aunque te costaría una paella.
lines.meaning: Of course! Although it would cost you a paella.

listening.meaning: If I were you, I'd leave now.
listening.note: Salir becomes saldría, with the stem saldr-.

listening.meaning: Could you close the window, please?
listening.note: The conditional makes a request polite.

listening.text: Me encantaría vivir cerca del puerto.
listening.meaning: I'd love to live near the harbour.
listening.note: New word: el puerto = the harbour.

listening.text: Mi hermano dijo que vendría a cenar.
listening.meaning: My brother said he would come to dinner.
listening.note: Dijo que + conditional: the future seen from the past.

listening.text: Yo en tu lugar, no diría nada a nadie.
listening.meaning: In your place, I wouldn't say anything to anybody.

listening.text: ¿Te importaría echarme una mano con estas cajas?
listening.meaning: Would you mind giving me a hand with these boxes?
listening.note: New word: la caja = the box.

listening.text: Cuando llegamos a casa, serían las doce de la noche.
listening.meaning: When we got home, it must have been about midnight.
listening.note: Serían: a guess about the past.

listening.text: Con más dinero, compraríamos una casa en el campo y tendríamos gallinas.
listening.meaning: With more money, we'd buy a house in the countryside and we'd have hens.
listening.note: New word: la gallina = the hen.

guide.tip: Stuck on a stem? Say the future first (tendré, saldré, haré), then swap -é for -ía.

bites.title: Would is -ía
bites.rule: Keep the whole infinitive and add -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían. Same endings for -ar, -er and -ir, always with an accent.

bites.title: Future stems, again
bites.rule: Irregular stems are the future's: tendr-, vendr-, pondr-, saldr-, sabr-, habr-, har-, dir-. Ir stays regular: iría.

bites.title: Advice and favours
bites.rule: Yo que tú / yo en tu lugar + conditional gives advice; ¿Podrías…? and ¿Te importaría + infinitive? ask nicely.
bites.example_meaning: If I were you, I'd leave now.

bites.title: Looking back
bites.rule: A guess about the past (serían las diez) and a past promise about the future (dijo que vendría) both take the conditional.
bites.example: Dijo que vendría a las ocho.
bites.example_meaning: She said she'd come at eight.

sorts.title: Future or conditional?
sorts.why: Both share the stem; the future ends in -é, -ás, -á…, the conditional in -ía, -ías, -ía…

sorts.title: What is the conditional doing?
sorts.why: Advice imagines your place; requests soften a question; guesses look back at what was probably true.

spots.sentence: Yo que tú, tenería más cuidado.
spots.why: Tener uses the future stem tendr-: tendría.

spots.sentence: Ayer me dijo que vendrá, pero no vino.
spots.why: Dijo que…: the future seen from the past becomes the conditional.
Every conditional ending has an accent on the í: viviríamos.
Hacer has the short stem har-: harías.
With an infinitive as the subject, encantar stays singular: me encantaría.

builds.text: Yo que tú, saldría más temprano.
builds.meaning: If I were you, I'd leave earlier.
Would you mind closing the door?

builds.text: Dijo que vendría a las ocho.
builds.meaning: He said he'd come at eight.

builds.text: Con más tiempo, viajaríamos por Europa.
builds.meaning: With more time, we'd travel around Europe.
